name: Aqua Obscura
about: A darkened underground chamber in which a screen of slowly changing coloured light is viewed through a pool. It sits among the garden's other works.
note: Inside the ticketed gardens near Penzance.

name: Atom
about: An atom-shaped steel structure on a hilltop above Wycoller, with panels that frame views of the Pennine moors.
note: Free; reached on foot from the nearest car park. Not verified on site.

name: Both nam Faileas (Hut of the Shadow)
about: A small hut on the Uist shore that projects an inverted image of the land and sky onto its inner wall.
note: Remote; check access and condition with Taigh Chearsabhagh.

photos.title: The Hut of the Shadows, Lochmaddy.jpg

name: Broomhill Sculpture Gardens
about: A large garden and woodland where sculptures are placed along a trail among trees and water.
note: Ticketed and open seasonally; position from OSM.

photos.title: Broomhill Sculpture gardens near Barnstaple - geograph.org.uk - 10309.jpg
Turning for Broomhill Sculpture Gardens - geograph.org.uk - 4609921.jpg

name: Cass Sculpture Foundation
about: A sculpture park of large contemporary works in a wooded landscape at Goodwood.
note: Open on set days; booking or ticket needed; check the Foundation website.

photos.artist: Leonora (Ellie) Enking from East Preston, United Kingdom
photos.title: CASS Sculptures (5166585895).jpg
Sculpture outside Cass Sculpture Foundation at Goodwood - geograph.org.uk - 2859092.jpg

name: Cells of Life
about: A set of sculpted grass mounds and shallow lakes shaped like cells and DNA strands, set in the grounds of Jupiter Artland.
note: Jupiter Artland charges entry and opens seasonally.

photos.title: Life Mounds by Charles Jencks - geograph.org.uk - 1990985.jpg
Life Mounds by Charles Jencks - geograph.org.uk - 1469171.jpg
Life Mounds by Charles Jencks - geograph.org.uk - 1469187.jpg

name: Colourfields
artist: Jo Rippon Architecture and Sophie Smallhorn
about: A viewpoint structure on the old cannon battery in Corporation Park, with coloured panels that tint the view of the town and moors beyond.
note: Free; in a public park on a hillside above Blackburn.

photos.title: Colourfields, the Panopticon in Corporation Park - geograph.org.uk - 6603058.jpg

name: Coppice Cloud Chamber
about: A woodland chamber built of coppiced wood, in a forest where the sky is seen reflected inside.
note: In woodland near Challock; position from OSM; verify before visiting.

photos.title: Coppice Cloud Chamber in King's wood - geograph.org.uk - 1092976.jpg

name: Cornwall Slate Line
about: A long line of Cornish slate set into the parkland at Chatsworth.
note: Chatsworth Park is open to walkers; find it near the sculpture routes in the park. Position from OSM.

name: Crawick Multiverse
about: A landscape of boulders, mounds and spirals laid out on a reclaimed coal-mining site, with its design based on the geometry of space and the cosmos.
note: Free to visit; paths are open year-round and a visitor centre operates in season.

photos.title: The Multiverse and Galaxies at the Crawick Multiverse.JPG

name: Deer Shelter Skyspace
about: An eighteenth-century brick deer shelter converted into a viewing room, with a rectangular opening cut in the roof that frames the sky above. A bench runs around the walls.
note: Inside Yorkshire Sculpture Park (free entry, charged parking). Best near dusk when the light inside changes.

photos.title: James Turrell, Deer Shelter Skyspace, 2006, Yorkshire Sculpture Park - geograph.org.uk - 3472776.jpg
Deer Shelter Skyspace by James Turrell, Yorkshire Sculpture Park - geograph.org.uk - 6895194.jpg

name: Dudley Millennium Sculpture Trail
about: A walk with public sculpture through the Dudley canal and quarry landscape.
note: Free; position from OSM.

name: Eden Cloud Chamber
about: A slate chamber that works like a camera obscura, throwing an upside-down image of the sky and trees onto its floor.
note: Inside the Eden Project, which charges entry.

name: Fingermaze
about: A thumbprint-shaped maze laid in slabs on the ground, a map of human trace on the land.
note: Public location; find at the position marked on the map.

photos.title: Hove Park Fingermaze viewed from walk path.jpg

name: Forest of Dean Sculpture Trail
artist: Various (Magdalena Jetelova, David Nash, Ian Hamilton Finlay and others)
about: A walking trail through the Forest of Dean with works set among the trees, including pieces by David Nash and Ian Hamilton Finlay. Several are made from wood, stone and metal.
note: Free to walk; parking charged at the Speech House end. Some works decay and are removed.

photos.title: Cathedral, Forest of Dean Sculpture Trail.jpg
Place - The Sculpture Trail Forest of Dean - geograph.org.uk - 1023452.jpg
Forest of Dean Sculpture Trail - geograph.org.uk - 6922331.jpg

name: Frank Bruce Sculpture Trail
about: Wooden figures and animals carved from local timber stand along a woodland path in the Cairngorms.
note: Position from OSM; verify before visiting.

photos.title: Frank Bruce Sculpture Trail, Feshiebridge - geograph.org.uk - 6062901.jpg
"Millennium" , sculpture on Frank Bruce Sculpture Trail - geograph.org.uk - 973856.jpg

name: Glenkiln Sculpture Park
about: Bronze figures by Henry Moore, Epstein and Rodin stand on open Galloway hillsides and by Glenkiln Reservoir. The works are placed to be found while walking.
note: Open farmland and country lanes; wear sensible shoes and respect livestock.

photos.title: Glenkiln Cross , by Henry Moore - geograph.org.uk - 223434.jpg
Henry Moore's 'King and Queen' in the Glenkiln Sculpture Park - geograph.org.uk - 952228.jpg

name: Grizedale Forest Sculpture
about: Dozens of woodland sculptures, many made on site from wood and stone, are hidden along forest trails among the trees. The programme has run since the 1970s.
note: Walk from the visitor centre; works come and go as they decay and are replaced.

photos.title: 'Between Elephants', a Grizedale Forest sculpture - geograph.org.uk - 4785168.jpg
"Stag Herd Roof", Grizedale Forest sculpture - geograph.org.uk - 4792621.jpg

name: Halo
about: A huge ring of steel panels, lit at night, on a hilltop above Rossendale. It is a landmark for a long way around.
note: Free; a hill walk onto the former landfill site above Haslingden.

name: Himalayan Garden and Sculpture Park
about: A garden with lakes, rhododendrons and a large collection of sculpture, mostly in stone.
note: Ticketed and open seasonally; position from OSM.

photos.title: The Himalayan Garden and Sculpture Park, Grewelthorpe - geograph.org.uk - 7225358.jpg

name: Horizon Line Chamber
about: A stone hut on the Morecambe Bay shore that projects the horizon onto its floor.
note: Sunderland Point is reached by a tidal causeway; check tide times before you go.

name: Irwell Sculpture Trail
place: Salford to Bacup, Greater Manchester and Lancashire
about: A trail of public art along the River Irwell valley from Salford to Rossendale, including large stone and metal works in former industrial land.
note: Free; use a map to join up the trail's separate sections.

photos.title: Stag sculpture on The Irwell Sculpture Trail .jpg

name: Kielder Skyspace (Cat Cairn)
place: Cat Cairn, Kielder Water & Forest Park
about: A small stone chamber on a hilltop with an open circular aperture in the roof, through which the changing sky is framed. Light changes inside it at dawn and dusk.
note: Reached by a forest walk from the Kielder Water & Forest Park roads; the light programme runs at dawn and dusk.

name: Landform Ueda
about: A stepped, spiralling earth mound with ponds, laid out in front of the Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art. Walkers can climb its curved terraces.
note: Free; in the grounds of the gallery on Belford Road.

photos.title: Landform by Charles Jencks at the Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art - geograph.org.uk - 4588097.jpg

name: Little Sparta
about: The poet-artist's own hillside garden, where inscribed stones, classical references and pools are set among grass and trees. It mixes poetry, humour and landscape.
note: Open on set days in summer, and visits are by timed ticket; check the Little Sparta Trust site.

name: Loch Ard Sculpture Trail
about: A forest trail with sculptures on Loch Ard's wooded shores and slopes.
note: Position from OSM; verify before visiting.

photos.title: The Sculpture Trail at Loch Ard - geograph.org.uk - 7471914.jpg

name: Macduff Circle
about: A circle of local stone laid out on the ground near Modern Two, in the manner of the artist's walk-based circles.
note: Free to see in the grounds.

name: Margam Park Sculpture
about: A country park with sculpture across its landscape beside the deer park.
note: Position is the country park centre (approximate).

name: Mud Maid and Giant's Head
about: A woman and a huge head of earth, clay and living plants, made as land sculpture in the Heligan gardens.
note: Inside the ticketed Heligan gardens; position approximate.

photos.title: The Mud Maid, Lost Gardens of Heligan - geograph.org.uk - 1464263.jpg
Mud Maid - The Lost Gardens of Heligan (9757695214).jpg
Mud Maid - Lost Gardens of Heligan - Cornwall, England - DSC02646.jpg

name: Northala Fields
about: Four large conical earth mounds built from construction rubble beside the A40, with spiral paths up to the summits and lakes at their feet.
note: Free park open all year; the largest mound gives long views over west London and Heathrow.

name: Northumberlandia
about: A huge landform shaped like a reclining woman, built from earth on the site of an opencast coal mine. Paths cross her body and up to her head, giving views over the Northumberland coalfield.
note: Free; walk paths over the whole body from the car park off Blagdon Lane.

name: Pendle Sculpture Trail
about: A trail of artworks around Pendle in the countryside of east Lancashire.
note: Position from OSM; check route details before visiting.

photos.title: Pendle Sculpture Trail, A field of witches' broomsticks - geograph.org.uk - 4535399.jpg

name: Ribble Valley Sculpture Trail (Brungerley Park)
about: A short trail of sculptures along the River Ribble in Brungerley Park at Clitheroe.
note: Position approximate; check on the ground for the current state of the works.

name: Rivers of Stone
about: A fingerprint-shaped installation in stone, referring to the veins of rivers in the Black Country landscape.
note: Public site in Dudley; position from OSM.

name: Sculpture by the Lakes
about: A private sculpture park set in lakes and gardens in Dorset, with large works placed around the water and lawns.
note: Ticketed and open on set days; check the park website before travelling.

photos.title: Sculpture By The Lakes, Pallington - geograph.org.uk - 3602322.jpg
Sculpture By The Lakes, Pallington - geograph.org.uk - 3602327.jpg
Sculpture By The Lakes, Pallington - geograph.org.uk - 3602318.jpg

name: Tewlwolow Kernow
about: An elliptical turf-covered chamber looking up through an oval opening to the sky. Evening programmes use coloured light on the interior walls.
note: Inside the ticketed gardens near Penzance; sky programmes at dawn and dusk need booking.

photos.title: Tremenheere - Skyspace - Tewlwolow Kernow by James Turrell - geograph.org.uk - 8422506.jpg

name: The Garden of Cosmic Speculation
about: A private garden filled with terraces, twisting landforms and sculptures inspired by ideas from physics and cosmology.
note: Opens to the public only on a few days a year through Scotland's Gardens Scheme; check before you travel.

photos.title: Portrack House, The Garden of Cosmic Speculation, Dumfries & Galloway.jpg

name: The Kelpies
about: Two 30-metre horse heads in stainless steel stand beside the Forth and Clyde Canal, a nod to the working horses of the area.
note: Free to view; guided tours of the interior need a ticket.

photos.title: The Kelpies at The Helix in Falkirk, Scotland, June 2014.jpg

name: The Singing Ringing Tree
about: A tree-shaped sculpture of galvanised steel pipes on the moor above Burnley. The wind blows across the pipes and makes it hum and sing.
note: Free; a short walk from the Crown Point car park. The sound is most striking in wind.

photos.title: Singing Ringing Tree near Burnley - geograph.org.uk - 5607531.jpg
The Singing Ringing Tree above Burnley - geograph.org.uk - 3346256.jpg
Singing Ringing Tree, Panopticon for Burnley - geograph.org.uk - 3346294.jpg

name: Tout Quarry Sculpture Park
about: A disused Portland stone quarry filled with carvings made on site by sculptors and stonemasons, among rocks, ramps and nature reserve habitat.
note: Free; paths can be uneven and working-quarry hazards remain in places.

photos.title: Carving at Tout Quarry Portland - geograph.org.uk - 4713615.jpg
DIY sculpture, Tout Quarry, Portland - geograph.org.uk - 5730291.jpg
Sculpture at Tout Quarry Portland - geograph.org.uk - 468783.jpg

name: Tyrebagger Cloud Chamber
about: A cloud chamber built in the woodland of Tyrebagger, near Aberdeen.
note: Position approximate (forest-level); check with Forestry and Land Scotland.

name: Wave Chamber
about: A stone chamber on the shore of Kielder Water whose mirror and lens throw the moving lake reflection onto the floor inside.
note: Reached from the Hawkhope car park; position approximate.

name: Yorkshire Sculpture Park
artist: Various (Henry Moore, Barbara Hepworth, James Turrell, David Nash and others)
about: A 500-acre country park of fields, woods and lakes where sculptures are set into the landscape. Its collection includes major works by Henry Moore, Barbara Hepworth and many contemporary artists.
note: Free to enter; parking is charged. Check opening hours for individual indoor galleries.

photos.title: Reclining Figure at Yorkshire Sculpture Park - geograph.org.uk - 519117.jpg
